qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the Delaware Division of Public Health for professional services related to the Delaware Health Fund FY 2028 Health Programs and Services. It includes a procurement schedule, submission instructions, eligibility requirements, scope of services, and evaluation criteria, clearly indicating a solicitation for proposals.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
This request for proposals (“RFP”) is issued pursuant to 29 Del. C. §§ 6981 and 6982.
Deadline for Receipt of Proposals Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT
A pre-bid meeting has NOT been scheduled for this Request for Proposal.

The following information shall be provided in each proposal in the order listed below. Failure to respond to any request for information within this proposal may result in rejection of the proposal at the sole discretion of the State.

findings.title: Subcontractor Approval and Identification Required
findings.fact: Subcontractors must be identified in the proposal and approved by the Division; the prime vendor remains fully responsible for performance.

quotes.quote: The proposed subcontractors must be approved by the Division of Public Health. Proposed subcontractors must be identified in the proposal; any subcontractor engaged after award must be approved in advance by the Division.

findings.title: Business References Required
findings.fact: Vendors must provide at least three business references of similar scope and value using Attachment 6.

quotes.quote: Provide  at  least  three  (3)  business  references  consisting  of  current  or  previous  customers  of  similar  scope  and  value  using  Attachment  6.

findings.title: Subcontractor Approval
findings.fact: Subcontractors must be identified in Attachment 7 and are subject to state approval; changes require prior written approval.

quotes.quote: Subcontractors, if any, shall be clearly identified in the Vendor’s proposal by completing Attachment 7, and are subject the approval and acceptance of Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) Division of Public Health.

findings.title: Vendor Responsibility for Subcontractors
findings.fact: The successful vendor is responsible for all products and services, including those provided by subcontractors.

quotes.quote: The successful Vendor(s) shall be responsible for all products and services as required by this RFP whether or not the Vendor or its subcontractor provided final fulfillment of the order.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: The contract shall not be assigned without express prior written consent from the Agency.

quotes.quote: Assignment – Any resulting contract shall not be assigned except by express prior written consent from the Agency.

findings.title: W-9 Registration Requirement
findings.fact: New vendors must complete registration through the Delaware Supplier Portal and have their Taxpayer ID matched with the IRS.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware requires a new vendor to complete the registration process through the Delaware Supplier Portal at http://esupplier.erp.delaware.gov. Successful completion of this registration enables the creation of a State of Delaware supplier record. The Taxpayer ID (SSN or EIN) and Applicant (supplier) name are submitted to the Internal Revenue Service for “matching”. If the Taxpayer ID and name do not match, the vendor record cannot be approved.

findings.title: Response to Questions Posted By
findings.fact: The Department's response to questions will be posted by September 3, 2026.

quotes.quote: Response to Questions Posted by:  Date: September 3, 2026

The Department’s response to questions will be posted, according to the procurement schedule, under the project listing in Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) and to the State of Delaware Bid Solicitation Directory Website: http://www.bids.delaware.gov/ by September 3, 2026.

findings.title: Proposal Expiration Date
findings.fact: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding at least through June 30, 2028.

quotes.quote: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding on the bidder at least through June 30, 2028.

findings.title: Quarterly 2nd Tier Report Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Accurate 2nd Tier reports shall be submitted to the contracting Agency’s contract manager on the 15th (or next business day) of the month following each quarterly period.

quotes.quote: Accurate 2nd Tier reports shall be submitted to the contracting Agency’s contract manager on the 15th (or next business day) of the month following each quarterly period.

findings.title: Evaluation Timeline
findings.fact: The evaluation of proposals is scheduled to occur from September 15 to October 9, 2026.

quotes.quote: Evaluation of Proposals Date: September 15 – October 9, 2026

findings.title: Evaluation Committee Discretion
findings.fact: The evaluation committee has sole discretion in accepting exceptions to the RFP requirements.

quotes.quote: Acceptance of exceptions is within the sole discretion of the evaluation committee.

findings.title: Evaluation of Proposals Begins Shortly After Due Date
findings.fact: Evaluation of proposals is expected to begin shortly after the proposal due date.

quotes.quote: Evaluation of the proposals is expected to begin shortly after the proposal due date.

findings.title: Evaluation Process Includes Clarification, References, and Oral Presentations
findings.fact: The Evaluation Team may contact vendors for clarification, may contact any customer for references, and may invite selected vendors for oral presentations that are scored or ranked.

quotes.quote: The Evaluation Team may contact any vendor in order to clarify uncertainties or eliminate confusion concerning the contents of a proposal. Proposals may not be modified as a result of any such clarification request.
The Evaluation Team may contact any customer of the vendor, whether or not included in the vendor’s reference list, and use such information in the evaluation process.

After initial scoring and a determination that vendor(s) are qualified to perform the required services, selected vendors may be invited to make oral presentations to the Evaluation Team. All vendor(s) selected will be given an opportunity to present to the Evaluation Team.

The selected vendors will have their presentations scored or ranked based on their ability to successfully meet the needs of the contract requirements, successfully demonstrate their product and/or service, and respond to questions about the solution capabilities.

findings.title: No Bid Bond or Performance Bond Required
findings.fact: There is no bid bond requirement and no performance bond requirement.

quotes.quote: There is no Bid Bond Requirement.
There is no Performance Bond requirement.

findings.title: Contract Execution Timeline
findings.fact: The successful vendor shall promptly execute a contract incorporating the terms of this RFP within twenty (20) days after award of the contract.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor shall promptly execute a contract incorporating the terms of this RFP within twenty (20) days after award of the contract.

findings.title: State's Right to Extend Contract
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to extend this contract on a month-to-month basis for a period of up to three months after the term of the full contract has been completed.

quotes.quote: The State reserves the right to extend this contract on a month-to-month basis for a period of up to three months after the term of the full contract has been completed.

findings.title: Vendor May Offer Lower Pricing
findings.fact: Vendors are not restricted from offering lower pricing at any time during the contract term.

quotes.quote: Vendors are not restricted from offering lower pricing at any time during the contract term.

findings.title: Cooperative Use of Award
findings.fact: The contract is available for use by other states and/or governmental entities through a participating addendum, but final approval resides with the Director of Government Support Services and places no obligation upon the awarded vendor.

quotes.quote: As a publicly competed contract awarded in compliance with 29 DE Code Chapter 69, this contract is available for use by other states and/or governmental entities through a participating addendum. Interested parties should contact the State Contract Procurement Officer identified in the contract for instruction. Final approval for permitting participation in this contract resides with the Director of Government Support Services and in no way places any obligation upon the awarded vendor(s).

findings.title: Contract Incorporates RFP and Vendor Response
findings.fact: This RFP and the selected vendor's response to this RFP will be incorporated as part of any formal contract.

quotes.quote: This RFP and the selected vendor’s response to this RFP will be incorporated as part of any formal contract.

findings.title: Liquidated Damages
findings.fact: The State may include liquidated damages provisions for non-performance in the final contract.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware may include in the final contract liquidated damages provisions for non-performance.

findings.title: Payment Terms
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to pay by ACH or P-Card; agencies will process payment within 30 days after receipt of correct invoice; vendors may offer discounts.

quotes.quote: The State reserves the right to pay by Automated Clearing House (ACH) or Purchase Card (P-Card). The agencies will authorize and process for payment of each invoice within thirty (30) days after the date of receipt of a correct invoice. Vendors are invited to offer in their proposal value added discounts (i.e. speed to pay discounts for specific payment terms).

findings.title: Billing Requirement
findings.fact: The successful vendor is required to 'Bill as Shipped' to the respective ordering agencies.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor is required to "Bill as Shipped" to the respective ordering agency(s).

findings.title: Contract Document Hierarchy
findings.fact: In case of discrepancy, the order of precedence is: contract, State's RFP, Vendor's response, purchase order.

quotes.quote: In the event there is any discrepancy between any of these contract documents, the following order of documents governs so that the former prevails over the latter: contract, State of Delaware’s RFP, Vendor’s response to the RFP and purchase order.

findings.title: Additional Terms and Conditions
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to add terms and conditions during contract negotiations.

quotes.quote: Additional Terms and Conditions – The State of Delaware reserves the right to add terms and conditions during the contract negotiations.

findings.title: Eligibility Limited to Private Organizations
findings.fact: This RFP is open only to private organizations; state-operated programs are not eligible to respond and must use a separate process.
findings.business_implication: State-operated programs are automatically disqualified from this RFP and must pursue a separate internal funding process. Private organizations have the opportunity to compete for funding.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm your organization's status as a private entity. If you are a state-operated program, do not submit a proposal; instead, follow the separate internal process. If private, ensure your proposal aligns with the RFP requirements.

quotes.quote: Eligibility:  This RFP is open to private organizations.  State-operated programs do not respond to this RFP; funding for state-operated programs is designated by the Department through a separate internal process pursuant to 16 Del. C. § 137(i)(1).
The Division of Public Health seeks proposals from private organizations for programs and services that advance the purposes of the Delaware Health Fund.

findings.title: Debarment and Suspension Disqualification
findings.fact: Any entity currently debarred or suspended is ineligible to bid, and any entity ineligible to conduct business in Delaware is ineligible to respond.
findings.business_implication: If your organization or any subcontractor is debarred, suspended, or otherwise ineligible to do business in Delaware, your proposal will be rejected. This is a strict disqualifier.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your organization and all proposed subcontractors are not on any debarment or suspension lists and are authorized to conduct business in Delaware. If any issues exist, address them before submitting.

quotes.quote: Any  individual,  business,  organization,  corporation,  consortium,  partnership,  joint  venture,  or any other entity including subcontractors currently debarred or suspended is ineligible to bid.  Any entity ineligible to conduct business in the State of Delaware for any reason is ineligible to respond to the RFP.

findings.title: Exclusions for Criminal Convictions and Ethical Violations
findings.fact: The evaluation team may refuse to consider proposals from vendors with certain criminal convictions, ethical violations, or poor contract performance.
findings.business_implication: A history of criminal convictions, ethical violations, or poor performance on contracts could lead to disqualification. This is a risk factor that may affect your eligibility.
findings.action_recommendation: Review your organization's history for any disqualifying events. If any exist, consider whether you can mitigate them or whether it is prudent to bid. Ensure all key personnel and subcontractors also meet these standards.

quotes.quote: The Proposal Evaluation Team reserves the right to refuse to consider any proposal from a vendor who: a. Has  been  convicted  for  commission  of  a  criminal  offense  as  an  incident  to  obtaining or attempting to obtain a public or private contract or subcontract, or in the performance of the contract or subcontract: b. Has  been  convicted  under  State  or  Federal  statutes  of  embezzlement,  theft,  forgery,  bribery,  falsification  or  destruction  of  records,  receiving  stolen  property,  or  other  offense  indicating  a  lack  of  business  integrity  or  business  honesty  that  currently  and  seriously  affects  responsibility  as  a  State  contractor: c. Has  been  convicted  or  has  had  a  civil  judgment  entered  for  a  violation  under  State  or  Federal  antitrust  statutes: d. Has  violated  contract  provisions  such  as:  1)   Known   failure   without   good   cause   to   perform   in   accordance   with   the   specifications  or  within  the  time  limit  provided  in  the  contract;  or  2)   Failure  to  perform  or  unsatisfactory  performance  in  accordance  with  terms  of  one  or  more  contracts; e. Has  violated  ethical  standards  set  out  in  law  or  regulation;  and f. Any  other  cause  listed  in  regulations  of  the  State  of  Delaware  determined  to  be  serious  and  compelling  as  to  affect  responsibility  as  a  State  contractor,  including  suspension  or  debarment  by  another  governmental  entity  for  a  cause  listed  in  the  regulations.

findings.title: State of Delaware Business Licensure Required
findings.fact: Prior to award, the successful vendor must furnish proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the application process.
findings.business_implication: You must be licensed to do business in Delaware before receiving an award. This is a prerequisite for contract execution.
findings.action_recommendation: If you do not already have a Delaware business license, start the application process immediately to avoid delays. Ensure you have the necessary documentation ready.

quotes.quote: Prior to the execution of an award document, the successful Vendor shall either furnish the Agency with proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the process of application where required.

Prior  to  receiving  an  award,  the  successful  vendor  shall  either  furnish  the  State  of  Delaware with proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the process of application where required.

findings.title: Joint Venture Restrictions
findings.fact: Multi-vendor proposals require a designated prime contractor; equal teaming arrangements are not accepted, and a primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal.
findings.business_implication: If you plan to team with other organizations, you must designate a prime contractor who will be solely responsible. Equal partnerships are not allowed, and you cannot be part of multiple proposals as a prime vendor.
findings.action_recommendation: If considering a joint venture, clearly define the prime contractor's role and responsibilities. Ensure that no organization is involved in more than one proposal as a prime. Review your teaming agreements to comply with these restrictions.

quotes.quote: Multi-vendor solutions (joint ventures) will be allowed only if one of the venture partners is designated as the “prime contractor”. The “prime contractor” must be the joint venture’s contact point for the State of Delaware and be responsible for the joint venture’s performance under the contract, including all project management, legal and financial responsibility for the implementation of all vendor systems.
The State of Delaware will not accept any proposals that reflect an equal teaming arrangement or from vendors who are co-bidding on this RFP.
A primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal in any form.

findings.title: No Offshore Activity Allowed
findings.fact: Vendors must not execute any activity in an offshore facility and must attest in their transmittal letter that no activity will take place outside the United States.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all work, including any subcontracting, is performed within the United States. This may impact the bidder's operational model, especially if they rely on offshore resources or have foreign offices. Failure to comply could lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Review all planned activities and subcontractors to confirm they are U.S.-based. Include a clear statement in the transmittal letter attesting to no offshore activity. If any offshore involvement exists, either adjust the plan or consider not bidding.

quotes.quote: No activity is to be executed in an offshore facility, either by a subcontracted firm or a foreign office or division of the vendor. The vendor must attest to the fact that no activity will take place outside of the United States in its transmittal letter. Failure to adhere to this requirement is cause for elimination from future consideration.

findings.title: Mandatory Proposal Components
findings.fact: Vendors must include specific forms and information in their proposal, including transmittal letter, pricing, vendor information, non-collusion, exceptions, confidentiality, business references, and workplan; failure to provide all may deem the vendor non-responsive.
findings.business_implication: The proposal must be complete with all required attachments and forms. Missing any component could result in the proposal being deemed non-responsive and rejected without evaluation. This increases the risk of disqualification due to administrative oversight.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a checklist of all mandatory submission items and ensure each is included and properly completed. Double-check that all forms are signed and all required information is provided. Consider having a second person review the submission for completeness before finalizing.

quotes.quote: The items listed above provide the basis for evaluating each vendor’s proposal. Failure to provide all appropriate information may deem the submitting vendor as “non-responsive” and exclude the vendor from further consideration.

findings.title: No Debarment or Suspension
findings.fact: Vendors must affirm that within the past five years, the firm and key individuals are not suspended or debarred.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must confirm that neither the company nor its key personnel have been suspended or debarred. This is a standard eligibility requirement; any history of debarment could disqualify the bidder.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct an internal review to ensure no current or past debarment or suspension exists for the firm or key individuals. If any issues are found, assess whether they can be resolved or if bidding is feasible. Otherwise, prepare the affirmation as required.

quotes.quote: The Vendor must affirm that within the past five (5) years the firm or any officer, controlling stockholder, partner, principal, or other person substantially involved in the contracting activities of the business is not currently suspended or debarred and is not a successor, subsidiary, or affiliate of a suspended or debarred business.

findings.title: Compliance with Laws
findings.fact: Vendors must certify compliance with all federal, state, and local laws, including non-collusion and ADA, and failure to comply may result in proposal disregard or contract termination.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure full compliance with all applicable laws, including non-collusion and ADA. Non-compliance could lead to proposal rejection or contract termination, posing legal and financial risks.
findings.action_recommendation: Review all applicable laws and regulations to ensure compliance. Specifically, verify that the proposal was independently prepared without collusion and that services will be ADA-compliant. Include the required certifications in the proposal.

quotes.quote: In submitting a proposal, Vendors certify that they comply with all federal, state and local laws applicable to their activities and obligations including: a. the laws of the State of Delaware; b. the applicable portion of the Federal Civil Rights Act of 1964; c. the Equal Employment Opportunity Act and the regulations issued there under by the federal government; d. a condition that the proposal submitted was independently arrived at, without collusion, under penalty of perjury; and e. that programs, services, and activities provided to the general public under resulting contract conform with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, and the regulations issued there under by the federal government. If any vendor fails to comply with a through e (noted above) of this paragraph, the State of Delaware reserves the right to disregard the proposal, terminate the contract, or consider the vendor in default.

findings.title: Production Environment Requirement
findings.fact: All hardware and software must be currently in use in a production environment by at least three other customers, have been in use for at least six months, and generally available for six months; unreleased or beta versions are not acceptable.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all proposed hardware and software are mature and proven in production environments. Using beta or unreleased versions is not allowed, which may limit the bidder's options and require using established products.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that all proposed products meet the production environment criteria. If any product is not yet generally available or lacks sufficient production references, consider substituting with a compliant alternative. Document the compliance in the proposal.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware requires that all hardware, system software products, and application software products included in proposals be currently in use in a production environment by at least three other customers, have been in use for at least six months, and have been generally available from the manufacturers for a period of six months. Unreleased or beta test hardware, system software, or application software will not be acceptable.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Deadline
findings.fact: All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.
findings.business_implication: This is a firm deadline; late submissions will be rejected. Missing it means the bidder will not be considered for the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all proposal documents are finalized and uploaded to the Euna Procurement portal well before the deadline. Allow ample time for file uploads and confirm submission via email receipt.

quotes.quote: All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.
Deadline for Receipt of Proposals  Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT

findings.title: Deadline for Questions
findings.fact: Questions must be submitted no later than August 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST.
findings.business_implication: This is the last opportunity to seek clarification on the RFP. Missing this deadline may leave ambiguities unresolved, potentially affecting proposal quality.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit all questions through the Euna Procurement portal before the deadline. Monitor the Q&A section for responses posted by September 3, 2026.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Questions  Date: August 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST
Questions may be submitted no later than August 28, 2026 @ 3:00 PM EST.

findings.title: Late Proposals Not Accepted
findings.fact: Proposals submitted after the specified date and time will not be accepted.
findings.business_implication: The portal will not accept late submissions, and the state will not consider them. This is a strict cutoff with no exceptions.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit well before the deadline to avoid technical issues. Verify that the submission is complete and confirmed by the portal's email receipt.

quotes.quote: Proposals submitted after the specified date and time will not be accepted by the Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) Portal.
Any proposal submitted after the Deadline for Receipt of Proposals date will not be accepted.

findings.title: Monthly Usage Report Submission Deadline
findings.fact: A complete and accurate Usage Report (Attachment 8) shall be furnished in an Excel format and submitted electronically, no later than the 15th (or next business day after the 15th day) of each month.
findings.business_implication: If awarded, the bidder must submit monthly usage reports by the 15th. Failure to do so could result in corrective action, cancellation of the award, or negative impact on future proposals.
findings.action_recommendation: Set up a recurring monthly reminder to prepare and submit the Usage Report by the 15th. Ensure the report is in the required Excel format and includes all required details.

quotes.quote: A complete and accurate Usage Report (Attachment 8) shall be furnished in an Excel format and submitted electronically, no later than the 15th (or next business day after the 15th day) of each month, detailing the purchasing of all items and/or services on this contract.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Online
findings.fact: Proposals shall be submitted online at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/
findings.business_implication: The only acceptable method of submission is through the Euna Procurement portal. Hard copies, email, or fax will not be accepted.
findings.action_recommendation: Create an account on the portal early and familiarize yourself with the submission process. Ensure all required documents are uploaded and the final submission is completed before the deadline.

quotes.quote: Proposals shall be submitted online at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria and Weighting
findings.fact: The RFP specifies six general evaluation requirements for proposals, but does not provide explicit weights or scoring methodology.
findings.business_implication: The lack of explicit weights or scoring methodology creates uncertainty about which evaluation criteria are most important. Bidders cannot optimize their proposals based on known priorities, and the State retains broad discretion in evaluating proposals.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should address all six evaluation criteria thoroughly and equally, ensuring each section is robust and well-documented. They should also monitor any addenda or Q&A for additional guidance on evaluation priorities.

quotes.quote: B. General Evaluation Requirements 1. Statement of Need (§ II.A of proposal)-Delaware-specific evidence of the health need and the service gap the program fills; for returning organizations, including prior-year results. 2. Alignment with Health Fund Priorities (§ II.B)-fit with the purposes in 16 Del. C. § 137(d), with the strongest weight for direct ties to tobacco prevention and cessation and to cancer prevention, detection, and treatment. 3. Program Design and Feasibility (§ II.C)-goals, activities, timeline, staffing, and geographic reach that are specific, coherent, and achievable within the contract year. 4. Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan (§ II.D)-specific, verifiable objectives with indicators, targets, and data sources, suitable for incorporation into the award agreement. 5. Organizational Capacity & Past Performance (§ II.E)-governance, financial management, audit history, and experience operating programs of similar scope. 6. Budget Reasonableness and Sustainability (§ II.F)= justified costs proportionate to reach, documented other funding, and a realistic plan given declining Master Settlement Agreement revenue.

findings.title: Award Not Necessarily Based on Highest Score
findings.fact: The State of Delaware is not obligated to award the contract to the vendor with the highest total point score; rather, the contract will be awarded to the vendor whose proposal is most advantageous to the State.
findings.business_implication: Even if a bidder submits a technically superior and highly scored proposal, the State may select another vendor based on its own assessment of what is 'most advantageous.' This introduces subjectivity and risk into the award decision.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should not rely solely on scoring high; they should also emphasize qualitative aspects such as alignment with State priorities, innovation, and overall value. They should craft a compelling narrative that demonstrates why their proposal is the most advantageous overall.

quotes.quote: It should be explicitly noted that the State of Delaware is not obligated to award the contract to the vendor who submits the lowest bid or the vendor who receives the highest total point score, rather the contract will be awarded to the vendor whose proposal is the most advantageous to the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Contract Term and Funding Contingency
findings.fact: The contract term is one year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation. Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right.
findings.business_implication: The contract is for a single year only, and continued funding is subject to annual appropriation and a new RFP process. This creates uncertainty for long-term planning and revenue stability.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should plan for a one-year engagement and consider the potential for re-compete. They should structure their proposal to deliver value within the initial term and be prepared to participate in future RFPs if they wish to continue.

quotes.quote: Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation. Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right: continued funding is subject to the annual statutory process under 16 Del. C. § 137(i), including the annual request for proposals, and to annual appropriation.

findings.title: Payment Only to Prime Vendor
findings.fact: The State will make contract payments only to the awarded vendor (prime vendor). Payments to subcontractors are the sole responsibility of the prime vendor.
findings.business_implication: The prime vendor bears full financial responsibility for subcontractor payments, which may impact cash flow and risk management. The State will not intervene in payment disputes with subcontractors.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should carefully assess subcontractor arrangements and ensure they have robust contract terms with subcontractors to mitigate payment risks. They should also consider the financial stability of subcontractors and include contingency plans.

quotes.quote: The State will make contract payments only to the awarded vendor. Payments to any-subcontractors are the sole responsibility of the prime vendor (awarded vendor).

findings.title: Costs and Payment Schedule
findings.fact: All contract costs must be detailed in the Vendor's cost proposal; no charges other than as specified in the proposal shall be allowed without written consent. Payment schedule based on milestones, no advance payments, and holdback up to 25% may be required.
findings.business_implication: The cost proposal must be comprehensive and accurate, as additional charges will not be permitted without State consent. The milestone-based payment schedule with potential 25% holdback may impact cash flow and require careful financial planning.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should meticulously prepare their cost proposal, ensuring all costs are included and justified. They should also plan for potential cash flow constraints by structuring milestones to align with project deliverables and negotiating acceptable holdback terms if possible.

quotes.quote: All contract costs must be detailed specifically in the Vendor’s cost proposal. No charges other than as specified in the proposal shall be allowed without written consent of the State of Delaware. The proposal costs shall include full compensation for all taxes that the selected vendor is required to pay.

The State of Delaware will require a payment schedule based on defined and measurable milestones. Payments for services will not be made in advance of work performed. The State of Delaware may require holdback of contract monies until acceptable performance is demonstrated (as much as 25%).

findings.title: Pricing Submission Requirement
findings.fact: Pricing must be submitted as identified in the solicitation, using Appendix F – Project Cost Template.
findings.business_implication: Failure to use the specified pricing template may render the proposal non-responsive and lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure pricing is prepared strictly in accordance with Appendix F – Project Cost Template and include all required cost details.

quotes.quote: Pricing as identified in the solicitation. Please submit your pricing/cost noted in Appendix F – Project Cost Template.

findings.title: Prime vendor solely responsible for contract performance
findings.fact: The prime vendor is solely responsible for fulfillment of any contract with the State, and the State will make contract payments only to the awarded vendor.
findings.business_implication: The bidder bears full contractual and financial responsibility, even if subcontractors are used; the State will not pay subcontractors directly.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess subcontractor reliability and ensure robust management and payment mechanisms are in place to avoid default.

quotes.quote: Any contract that may result from this RFP shall specify that the prime vendor is solely responsible for fulfillment of any contract with the State as a result of this procurement.
The State will make contract payments only to the awarded vendor.

findings.title: Vendor responsible for subcontractor work quality and performance
findings.fact: The vendor selected shall be solely responsible for contractual performance and management of all subcontract relationships, assuming all responsibility for work quality, delivery, installation, maintenance, and any supporting services required by a subcontractor.
findings.business_implication: Any subcontractor failure will be the bidder's responsibility, potentially leading to financial and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct thorough due diligence on subcontractors, define clear performance expectations, and include indemnification clauses in subcontracts.

quotes.quote: The vendor selected shall be solely responsible for contractual performance and management of all subcontract relationships. This contract allows subcontracting assignments; however, vendors assume all responsibility for work quality, delivery, installation, maintenance, and any supporting services required by a subcontractor.

findings.title: ACA hold harmless and indemnification
findings.fact: Vendor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and defend the State to the maximum extent of any liability arising out of determinations that the State is a dual or sole employer of temporary staff for ACA purposes.
findings.business_implication: The bidder could face significant financial exposure if the State is deemed an employer under the ACA, including legal defense costs and liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Evaluate the potential ACA risks, ensure compliance with ACA requirements for temporary staff, and consider obtaining appropriate insurance coverage.

quotes.quote: In the event that the Internal Revenue Service, or any other third party governmental entity determines that the State of Delaware is a dual employer or the sole employer of any individual temporary staff person(s) provided to the State of Delaware pursuant to this Solicitation, Vendor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and defend the State to the maximum extent of any liability to the State arising out of such determinations.

findings.title: Vendor responsible for all costs and liabilities as independent contractor
findings.fact: Each party shall be responsible for compliance with all applicable workers compensation, unemployment, disability insurance, social security withholding and all other similar matters, and neither party shall be liable for any debts, accounts, obligations or other liability whatsoever of the other party.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must bear all employment-related costs and liabilities for its own personnel, with no recourse against the State.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure proper payroll, tax, and insurance arrangements are in place for all staff, and budget for these costs in the pricing.

quotes.quote: Each party shall be responsible for compliance with all applicable workers compensation, unemployment, disability insurance, social security withholding and all other similar matters. Neither party shall be liable for any debts, accounts, obligations or other liability whatsoever of the other party or any other obligation of the other party to pay on the behalf of its employees or to withhold from any compensation paid to such employees any social benefits, workers compensation insurance premiums or any income or other similar taxes.

findings.title: Vendor responsible for costs of licenses and permits
findings.fact: The cost of permits and other relevant costs required in the performance of the contract shall be borne by the successful vendor.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must factor in the cost of obtaining and maintaining all necessary licenses and permits into their pricing. Failure to do so could result in unexpected expenses and potential non-compliance.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify all required licenses and permits for the contract, estimate their costs, and include them in the cost proposal. Ensure compliance with Delaware state and local regulations.

quotes.quote: The cost of permits and other relevant costs required in the performance of the contract shall be borne by the successful vendor.

findings.title: Warranty Obligation
findings.fact: Vendor must provide a one-year warranty and correct any defects at its own expense.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is obligated to provide a one-year warranty and fix any defects at no additional cost to the State. This could lead to significant post-acceptance costs if the system has issues.
findings.action_recommendation: Allocate sufficient resources and budget for warranty support. Ensure the system is thoroughly tested before acceptance to minimize defects. Consider the warranty costs in the pricing strategy.

quotes.quote: The Vendor will provide a warranty that the deliverables provided pursuant to the contract will function as designed for a period of no less than one (1) year from the date of system acceptance. The warranty shall require the Vendor to correct, at its own expense, the setup, configuration, customizations or modifications so that it functions according to the State’s requirements.

findings.title: Termination for Cause
findings.fact: State may terminate for cause with 20 days notice, and vendor may have 5 days to respond.
findings.business_implication: The State can terminate the contract for cause with 20 days' notice, and the vendor has only 5 days to respond. This gives the State significant leverage and could lead to abrupt termination if the vendor fails to meet obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure strict compliance with all contract terms and deadlines. Have a rapid response plan in place to address any potential violations within the 5-day window. Consider negotiating for a longer response period.

quotes.quote: If, for any reasons, or through any cause, the Vendor fails to fulfill in timely and proper manner its obligations under this Contract, or if the Vendor violates any of the covenants, agreements, or stipulations of this Contract, the State shall thereupon have the right to terminate this contract by giving written notice to the Vendor of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.
On receipt of the contract cancellation notice from the State, the Vendor shall have no less than five (5) days to provide a written response and may identify a method(s) to resolve the violation(s).

findings.title: Termination for Convenience
findings.fact: State may terminate for convenience with 20 days notice, and vendor receives compensation for satisfactory work.
findings.business_implication: The State can terminate the contract at any time with 20 days' notice, but the vendor will be compensated for work completed and usable to the State. This provides some financial protection but may still result in lost expected profits.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain detailed records of all work completed and deliverables to ensure proper compensation in case of termination. Consider including provisions for payment of non-usable work or other costs in the contract.

quotes.quote: The State may terminate this Contract at any time by giving written notice of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination. In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, models, photographs, reports, supplies, and other materials shall, at the option of the State, become its property and the Vendor shall be entitled to receive compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials, and which is usable to the State.

findings.title: Covenant against Contingent Fees
findings.fact: Vendor warrants no contingent fees; breach allows contract annulment or fee recovery.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that no contingent fees have been paid to secure the contract. If such fees are discovered, the State can annul the contract or recover the fees, which could be financially damaging.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct an internal review to ensure compliance with this covenant. Maintain documentation to prove that no contingent fees were paid. Be aware of the severe consequences of breach.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor will warrant that no person or selling agency has been employed or retained to solicit or secure this contract upon an agreement of understanding for a commission or percentage, brokerage or contingent fee excepting bona-fide employees, bona-fide established commercial or selling agencies maintained by the Vendor for the purpose of securing business. For breach or violation of this warranty the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul the contract without liability or at its discretion to deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: Background Check Violation Penalty
findings.fact: Violation of background check requirements may result in contract cancellation for cause.
findings.business_implication: Non-compliance with background check requirements can lead to termination of the contract for cause, which may result in financial losses, reputational damage, and potential legal claims.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust background check procedures for all employees and subcontractors who will have access to state property or contact with vulnerable populations. Maintain documentation of compliance and be prepared to provide lists and certifications upon request.

quotes.quote: A violation of this condition represents a violation of the contract terms and conditions, and may subject the Vendor to penalty, including contract cancellation for cause.

findings.title: Work Product Ownership
findings.fact: All materials developed under contract are sole property of the State.
findings.business_implication: Any intellectual property or materials created during the contract will be owned exclusively by the State, limiting the vendor's ability to reuse or exploit such work for other clients or purposes.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the scope of 'materials and products' and negotiate for a license or rights to use the work product for internal purposes or future projects, if possible. Ensure that any pre-existing materials are clearly identified and excluded from the ownership clause.

quotes.quote: All materials and products developed under the executed contract by the vendor are the sole and exclusive property of the State.

findings.title: Applicable Law and Jurisdiction
findings.fact: Delaware law applies and vendor consents to jurisdiction in Delaware.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must comply with Delaware laws and may be required to litigate disputes in Delaware courts, which could be inconvenient and costly if the vendor is located outside Delaware.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the implications of Delaware jurisdiction and consider whether it is acceptable. If not, attempt to negotiate for a different venue or choice of law, though this may be difficult in a government contract. Ensure legal counsel is familiar with Delaware law.

quotes.quote: The laws of the State of Delaware shall apply, except where Federal Law has precedence. The successful vendor consents to jurisdiction and venue in the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Audit Disallowances
findings.fact: Vendor bears cost of audit disallowances.
findings.business_implication: If the State audits the vendor's financial records and disallows certain costs, the vendor must reimburse the State from its own resources, potentially reducing profit margins and impacting cash flow.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain meticulous financial records and ensure all costs charged to the contract are allowable and properly documented. Implement internal controls to prevent disallowances and be prepared for potential audits.

quotes.quote: The cost of any Contract audit disallowances resulting from the examination of the Vendor's financial records will be borne by the Vendor.

findings.title: Criminal/Civil Sanctions for FTI Disclosure
findings.fact: Unauthorized disclosure of FTI may result in fines and imprisonment.
findings.business_implication: Employees handling Federal Tax Information (FTI) face severe criminal penalties for unauthorized disclosure, including fines up to $5,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, as well as civil damages. This imposes a high compliance burden on the vendor.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop and enforce strict policies for handling FTI, including training, confidentiality agreements, and access controls. Ensure all employees with access to FTI are properly certified and recertified annually. Implement monitoring to prevent unauthorized disclosures.

quotes.quote: Each officer or employee of a contractor to whom FTI is or may be disclosed shall be notified in writing that FTI disclosed to such officer or employee can be used only for a purpose and to the extent authorized herein, and that further disclosure of any FTI for a purpose not authorized herein constitutes a felony punishable upon conviction by a fine of as much as $5,000 or imprisonment for as long as 5 years, or both, together with the costs of prosecution.

findings.title: State's Right to Terminate Negotiations
findings.fact: The State of Delaware may terminate negotiations at any time and for any reason, or for no reason.
findings.business_implication: The State has no obligation to continue negotiations, and can walk away at any point without liability. This creates significant uncertainty for the bidder, as time and resources invested in negotiations may not lead to a contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should avoid making substantial investments or commitments based on the assumption that negotiations will lead to a contract. They should also ensure that any costs incurred during the negotiation phase are not recoverable, and consider including a clause in their internal planning to mitigate risks associated with potential termination.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware may terminate negotiations at any time and for any reason, or for no reason.

findings.title: Evaluation Team May Terminate Negotiations
findings.fact: The Proposal Evaluation Team may, at its discretion, terminate negotiations with any or all vendors.
findings.business_implication: The Evaluation Team has the sole discretion to end negotiations with any vendor at any time, meaning the bidder could be dropped from the process even if they are performing well. This adds another layer of uncertainty and risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should maintain a competitive edge throughout the negotiation process and be prepared for the possibility of termination. They should also seek to understand the Evaluation Team's criteria and priorities to align their proposal and negotiation strategy accordingly.

quotes.quote: The Team may negotiate with one or more vendors during the same period and may, at its discretion, terminate negotiations with any or all vendors.

findings.title: Vendor Must Terminate Employment of Ineligible Employee
findings.fact: If a vendor discovers they have employed a person who cannot legally accept employment under state or federal law, they must terminate that employment immediately.
findings.business_implication: The vendor is responsible for ensuring all employees are legally eligible to work. Failure to terminate an ineligible employee immediately could lead to contract termination or legal penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should implement robust employment verification processes to ensure all employees are legally authorized to work. They should also have a clear procedure in place to promptly terminate any employee found to be ineligible, to comply with this requirement.

quotes.quote: If a vendor discovers that they have done so, they must terminate that employment immediately.

findings.title: State's Right to Annul Contract for Lobbying or Gratuities
findings.fact: The State of Delaware shall have the right to annul any contract resulting from this RFP without liability if the vendor breaches the warranty against lobbying or gratuities.
findings.business_implication: Any violation of the lobbying or gratuities prohibition can result in the contract being annulled without any liability to the State, and the vendor may also face financial penalties. This is a serious risk that could lead to loss of the contract and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders must strictly comply with all lobbying and gratuity restrictions. They should establish internal policies and training to ensure all employees and agents understand and adhere to these rules. Additionally, they should avoid any actions that could be perceived as lobbying or providing gratuities to State employees.

quotes.quote: For breach or violation of this warranty, the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul any contract resulting from this RFP without liability or at its discretion deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: State's Right to Cancel Solicitation
findings.fact: The State of Delaware reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time during the procurement process, for any reason or for no reason.
findings.business_implication: The entire procurement process can be cancelled at any time, meaning the bidder's efforts in preparing and submitting a proposal may be wasted. There is no guarantee that a contract will be awarded.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should weigh the potential costs of proposal preparation against the risk of cancellation. They should also monitor any updates or addenda to the RFP for signs of potential cancellation and be prepared to pivot resources if the solicitation is cancelled.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time during the procurement process, for any reason or for no reason.

findings.title: Termination for Convenience
findings.fact: The State may terminate the contract at any time for convenience with at least 20 days' written notice. The Vendor is entitled to compensation for satisfactory work completed that is usable to the State.
findings.business_implication: The State can end the contract without cause, but the Vendor will be compensated for completed work that the State can use. This reduces the risk of uncompensated work if the State decides to terminate early.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain detailed records of all work performed and deliverables, and ensure that all work products are of high quality and usable to the State to maximize compensation in case of termination.

quotes.quote: The State may terminate this Contract at any time by giving written notice of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.

In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, models, photographs, reports, supplies, and other materials shall, at the option of the State, become its property and the Vendor shall be entitled to receive compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials, and which is usable to the State.

findings.title: Termination for Non-Compliance with Laws
findings.fact: If the Vendor fails to comply with certain laws, the State reserves the right to terminate the contract.
findings.business_implication: Non-compliance with applicable laws (including civil rights, equal employment, and ADA) can lead to termination, which could result in loss of revenue and damage to the Vendor's reputation.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure strict compliance with all federal, state, and local laws, and maintain documentation of compliance efforts. Regularly review legal obligations and implement training for staff to avoid violations.

quotes.quote: If any vendor fails to comply with a through e (noted above) of this paragraph, the State of Delaware reserves the right to disregard the proposal, terminate the contract, or consider the vendor in default.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Submit Reports
findings.fact: Failure to submit required monthly usage reports may result in corrective action, up to and including cancellation of the award.
findings.business_implication: Missing monthly reports can lead to contract cancellation, which would stop revenue and could affect future opportunities with the State.
findings.action_recommendation: Set up a reliable process to submit accurate monthly usage reports on time, using the provided template. Assign responsibility and set reminders to ensure compliance.

quotes.quote: Any exception to this mandatory requirement or failure to submit complete reports, or in the format required, may result in corrective action, up to and including the possible cancellation of the award.

findings.title: Conflict in Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting Date
findings.fact: The RFP schedule states the Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting is on November 6, 2026, but the Notice of Award section states it will be held no later than November 7, 2026.
findings.business_implication: The discrepancy in the meeting date could cause confusion about the timeline, potentially affecting the Vendor's ability to prepare for the meeting or respond to any changes.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the exact date with the State procurement officer to ensure alignment. Monitor official communications for any updates and plan accordingly.

quotes.quote: Health Fund Advisory Committee Public Meeting   Date: November 6, 2026
reviewed by the Health Fund Advisory Committee at a public meeting with public testimony no later than November 7, 2026

findings.title: Conflict in Final Recommended Award List Transmittal Date
findings.fact: The RFP schedule states the Final Recommended Award List Transmitted date is November 13, 2026, but the Notice of Award section states it will be transmitted no later than November 15, 2026.
findings.business_implication: The conflicting dates for the final award list transmission could lead to uncertainty about when the Vendor will know if they are selected, impacting planning and resource allocation.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the State on the official date. Prepare for the possibility of either date and stay in contact with the procurement office for updates.

quotes.quote: Final Recommended Award List Transmitted:   Date: November 13, 2026

transmitted as a final recommended award list to the Governor, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Controller General, and the members of the Joint Finance Committee no later than November 15, 2026.

findings.title: Conflict in Subcontracting Allowed
findings.fact: The RFP states that subcontracting is allowed in one section, but another section states that services shall not be subcontracted without prior written approval, which is not a direct contradiction but could be ambiguous.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity may lead to misunderstandings about the subcontracting process, potentially causing compliance issues or disputes during contract execution.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the contracting officer the exact subcontracting approval process and ensure all subcontractors are identified and approved in writing before contract signing.

quotes.quote: The use of subcontractors WILL be permitted for this project.
Services specified in the proposal shall not be subcontracted without prior written approval by the State of Delaware

findings.title: Contract Term and Renewal Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFP states the contract term is one year (July 1, 2027 – June 30, 2028) but also mentions a Fiscal Year 2029 RFP and a streamlined continuation response, creating ambiguity about the actual contract duration and renewal process.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity may affect resource planning and financial projections, as the actual contract duration and renewal process are unclear.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek written clarification from the State regarding the contract term, renewal process, and the relationship between the FY2028 contract and the FY2029 RFP.

quotes.quote: Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation.

Organizations funded in Fiscal Year 2028 that seek Fiscal Year 2029 funding must respond to the Fiscal Year 2029 RFP (anticipated release on or before July 1, 2027), which is expected to include a streamlined continuation response for organizations proposing to continue substantially the same program.

findings.title: Contract Document Precedence Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFP states that the contract documents include the RFP, purchase order, executed contract, and supplemental documents, but the order of precedence lists 'contract' first, then RFP, vendor response, and purchase order. This creates ambiguity about the exact hierarchy, especially since the purchase order is listed last but is also described as the authorization to proceed.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity in document precedence could lead to disputes over which terms prevail in case of inconsistencies, potentially affecting contract interpretation and performance.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the order of precedence with the State and ensure that all contractual documents are consistent to avoid future conflicts.

quotes.quote: The RFP, the purchase order, the executed contract and any supplemental documents between the State of Delaware and the successful vendor shall constitute the contract between the State of Delaware and the vendor. In the event there is any discrepancy between any of these contract documents, the following order of documents governs so that the former prevails over the latter: contract, State of Delaware’s RFP, Vendor’s response to the RFP and purchase order.
The purchase order shall serve as the authorization to proceed in accordance with the bid specifications and the special instructions, once it is received by the successful vendor.

findings.title: Termination for Convenience Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFP mentions termination for convenience in the context of funding exhaustion, but also states that termination due to exhaustion of funds is not a termination for convenience. This creates ambiguity about the nature of termination when funds are exhausted.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity may affect the vendor's rights and remedies in the event of termination due to funding exhaustion, potentially leading to disputes over compensation.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the State on the termination provisions, specifically the implications of funding exhaustion and the vendor's rights in such a scenario.

quotes.quote: exhaustion of funds. This is not a termination for convenience and will not be converted to such.
This is not a termination for convenience and will not be converted to such.
